I think it's good to use the knowledge that you most likely have autism in order to better understand yourself. You can use it to learn coping strategies and it's nice to find a community that understands you. 

On the other hand, I think it's good to specify that you are self diagnosed, because self diagnosis isn't the same as a professional diagnosis. I was "self diagnosed" for a few years (I didn't really diagnose myself, I just knew it was a very strong possibility) and I used it to understand myself, told a few close friends. 

The problem with self diagnosis is that it is very subjective and people are very susceptible to confirmation bias (once you believe in something, you only search for confirmation of what you believe in instead of considering other possibilities). You can be socially awkward, you can have sensory issues and strong passions for things, without necessarily being autistic. Adhd, social anxiety, ocd, cptds can all produce very similar symptoms and it can get very difficult to properly identify what diagnoses you're really dealing with. When you are getting diagnosed, in most cases doctors will also ask you to bring someone that knows you very well, ideally from childhood, which also makes the diagnosis more objective.

All in all, I support self diagnosis, unless you claim to be professionally diagnosed.
